messages:
izzy: Quick design review for the private setup wizardnetwork step. I pushed a prototype where we progressively disclose details: summary row -> details panel -> optional network map. Wanted feedback on keyboard-first flows and copy.

noah: Progressive disclosure sounds good for onboarding customers. One question: when a probe fails, should details auto-open or just highlight the summary? Auto-open helps novices but can be noisy for power users.

reema: Proposal: open on first failure only during the session, then leave collapsed for subsequent runs. Add a small 'pin open' toggle on the probe so users can keep it expanded.

chris: Accessibility: pin control must be keyboard operable and remember user preference per browser (localStorage) rather than per-account to avoid cross-session surprises. Also ensure pin has aria-pressed state.

izzy: Good. Microcopy: current root failure line reads 'network check failed'  which is too generic. Option A: 'Connectivity check failed  agent could not reach Redwood control plane. Verify SSH (22) and allowed CIDRs.' Option B (less technical): 'Can't reach Redwood from agent  check firewall or network settings.' Thoughts?

sylvie: A/B test both. Also prepare a concise translation-friendly version for i18n teams: no punctuation-heavy sentences and avoid idioms. E.g., 'Agent cannot reach Redwood. Verify SSH port 22 and allowed CIDR ranges.'

reema: Also a privacy/consent note: the preflight runs egress probes that reveal the agent's egress IP. We should surface a tiny disclosure: 'Probes may reveal your agent egress IP to Redwood for diagnostics' with a link to privacy docs. Designers, how to show without clutter?

izzy: Maybe a small i icon inline next to 'Run probes' with tooltip text and a 'Learn more' link. Keep it collapsed by default.

noah: Visual: in dark mode the error amber used for warnings is low contrast. Use full-bleed left accent + icon + bold label, not just color. Add underline or box when needed. Contrast check needed.

chris: Keyboard flows: when user presses Enter on summary row, expand and move focus to the first interactive element inside details (Retry probe). But only do this if the expansion was user-initiated; avoid focus shift for programmatic opens. Use focus management helpers.

reema: Logs UX: parse first, raw second. Add a copyable 'support snippet' button that composes a short prefilled text blob with the probe name, timestamp, parsed error, and a link to 'copy raw logs' so support can paste quickly. This reduces back-and-forth.

sylvie: Love that. Ensure the snippet is localizable and minimal. Example snippet: 'SSH probe failed (timeout). Last checked: 2m ago. Parsed: connection timed out. Raw: [copied separately]'.

izzy: Regarding remediation CTAs: change 'Help' to 'View remediation steps' and make that deep-link to anchors. Also add a contextual quick action 'Test from this network' that gives a curl example the user can run from the agent host.

noah: For flaky infra, show a small trend sparkline in the summary row (last 5 runs) so users can instantly see intermittency. Keep it tiny and accessible (provide textual tooltip like '3/5 failed').

chris: Animation/accessibility: any attention animation (pulse/shake) must respect prefers-reduced-motion and be subtle. Add a CSS reduced-motion query and avoid layout-shifting effects.

reema: QA checklist for handoff: 1) pin stored in localStorage; 2) aria-pressed for pin; 3) aria-live polite scoped to the row; 4) focus on Retry only for user-initiated expand; 5) privacy tooltip present with link; 6) dark mode contrast >=4.5:1; 7) support-snippet generates sanitized output.

sylvie: I'll write the short copy variants and a translation note. Izzy can update Figma.

izzy: I'll iterate the prototype (progressive disclosure + sparkline + support-snippet) and post a Loom. Meeting in 20 to review. ux-bot: Saved mock: https://figma.com/mock/prog-disclose-123 (placeholder).

noah: Thanks all :thumbsup:
